utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Now we were still concluding, Mr. Mettraux, some exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see you are repositioned for today but I must call on you first.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Our colleagues have been promoted, I think, Your Honour. The next document to be tendered was Rule 65 ter 1D715. This was the White House statement which accompanied the presidential order of 26 of June of 2001, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The one earlier press statement was included despite our hesitation because of a possibility that it may not have been adequately reflected in the transcript. I don't think that can be said of this one. The cross-examination on this one is clear. So the Chamber's view is that this should not be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I simply wish to make it clear, Your Honour, this is an official statement. If I said press, it wasn't a press article, simply to make it clear it was an official statement from the White House.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. What does that establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. The next document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You understand what I mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There could be official statements from 50 governments in the world. They're not going to help us decide any particular facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document which the Defence would seek to tender is Rule 65 ter 1D118 and that is the conclusion of the council meeting of the EU dated 16 and 17 of 2001, to which an annex is attached which is a recommendation and conclusion raised by the council of the European Union. It is dated the 16 and 17 of July of 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D237, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is Rule 65 ter 1D807. This is a bulletin of non-compliance with the cease-fire. You will recall that it came from the Prosecution through the OSCE archives and the issue which had been put to the witness in relation to this document was the sandbagging of the mosque in the village of Nikustak in which the headquarters of this brigade was located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I would raise the same concern than with the other document yesterday. There is like an extract with different entries and the witness was only shown a particular entry about one particular day on two times. So if my learned colleague seeks to tender this document, I will actually to focus on this particular entry not the whole bulletin.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'd be happy, Your Honour, to seek to tender only the first page if we can make arrangements with the registry to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But is not the content that you're interested in reflected in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would not receive the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is one of the documents which was mentioned originally at the start of the hearing in the absence of the witness. It's Rule 65 ter 1D817, and it relates to a record made by a particular embassy or transmitted through a particular embassy as regards the setting on fire of houses and churches in, or at least one church, in the village of Matejce, which was again the headquarters of the brigade of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Again, I ask the question, is not that reflected fully in your questioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We hope it is, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will not be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D823. This is a so-called spot report dated the 6th of March of 2001 and it comes from the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the justification for us receiving it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document that was put to the witness in response to his claim that members of the NLA were at all times wearing uniforms. Documents reveal to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that issue was fully ventilated with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will not be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D811. This was a report of the 3rd Guardist Brigade of the Macedonian army, which is a record, effectively, of the incident in Ljubotenski Bacila. It is dated the 10th of August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D238, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There was one more document, Your Honour, but in view of your previous ruling, we will not seek to tender this one. That will be all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will understand that we're concerned to ensure that we don't clutter the record with documents that have been adequately dealt with in cross-examination or examination-in-chief and the contents of which that are material to this case are already reflected fully in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just a small comment with regard to these last documents that has been tendered. It was actually produced by a former witness, Mr. Despodov, and just to indicate for the record that it was not put to him during cross-examination and not tendered through this witness in cross-examination by my learned colleague. Just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying that it is already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No. I'm saying that it is not an exhibit, but it's a document produced by General Despodov who was a witness here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And during the cross-examination it was not put to him and it was not tendered through him. So I'm just stating that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. This repositioning of the Defence is due to technical reasons because we wish to use some video-clips and only the front line of the Defence can resort to using them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. My name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with Jasmina Zivkovic, we are the Defence counsel of Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before I begin my questioning, I wish to point out to you that you perhaps understand my language in which I will pose you the question, but I will ask you nonetheless for interpretation to be done on the part of the interpreters that these questions be interpreted into your own language and to respond duly afterwards, all with the aim of avoiding overlap, my questions with your answers. Are we ready to begin, Witness?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were born in Skopje on 29th of December, 1967. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You finished your primary education in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In 1987, in January, you graduated from the Military Academy in Sarajevo. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo and in Croatia, in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us which speciality and military branch of the academy did you finish?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In anti-aircraft, radar operator, controlling the aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You told us that after completing the academy you assumed the rank Sergeant. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this mean that you did not complete a Military Academy but, rather, secondary military school?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The middle military school was in Sarajevo; and I completed half of the Military Academy in Zadar, of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that if you had completed the academy, the first rank would you have received would be lieutenant, second lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military -- the military school was four years in Sarajevo, and it was one year in Zadar that I completed. And you would receive that rank only if you completed four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You would concur with me that you had not finished the military academy as you had stated previously?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends how that was understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, you decisively state and now you confirm that you completed the Military Academy. Under Military Academy, I understand, a faculty, a military faculty which is contrary to your response that followed.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- my -- my aim wasn't to -- to say what I graduated, but I was telling you how many years I studied where.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. As of February 1992, you began working in the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was April or May, because in 1992 I left the Yugoslav army and that was in February.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As an ethnic Albanian, then, without any problems due to ethnic affiliations, you found employment in the army of the Republic of Macedonia immediately after the Republic of Macedonia became independent and its army was formed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was one of those 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us which rank you had in the Macedonian army in 2001, prior to your leaving the army?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: B Sergeant.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you concur with me that you advanced in your service, during your service in the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was promoted, but it was late, very late.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001, Zejadin Tushi, an ethnic Albanian, was the director of the headquarters of the Republic of Macedonia with General Major rank and the third person in the military hierarchy in the army?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001, Brigadier-General Fadil Gazafer, an ethnic Albanian was commander of the 1st Infantry Brigade, which was the only professional unit in the army of the Republic of Macedonia, and later became the deputy of the Chiefs of Staff of the army which -- a position which he holds to this day?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that Fadil Gazafer was the commander, but he was not Albanian. He has declared himself as Turkish.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001, the chief of G-5 of the General Staff the sector for mobilisation was Colonel Naser Sejdini, an ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser who? Naser Sejdini.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Naser Sejdini.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he's a military officer but I don't know that he holds that position, as chief of G-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that many of the head positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were held by ethnic Albanians which is contrary to your testimony before this esteemed Court, that Albanians were not able to advance in their professions because of their ethnic affiliation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, sir. Because there were also officers from the former Yugoslavia and it was a continuation then from the army of the former Yugoslavia and you cannot compare by quoting only one or two Albanian officers as having those ranks. I said it a day earlier. It is not important whether you are a minister or a deputy minister. It -- irrespective of your ethnicity. But the numbers should be in line with the percentages of the population, which is roughly 25 percent.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Nonetheless, my question is: Regarding 2001, which is ten years after the independence of Macedonia, surely this automatism after ten years would have not ensured them these positions, rather, that these were received by promotions. Can you agree with me on this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's normal, on the basis of the period you've been working in that profession and on that basis you get the ranks. But you're talking about two or three persons. We should be talking about the proportion of representation in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: To my learned colleague from the Prosecution you responded that after the first parliamentary election, the government began discriminating the Albanians. To my colleague Mr. Mettraux he pointed out there were members of parliament, Albanians after the first parliamentary elections in the independent Macedonia. More than 20 per cent, it was said. Is it correct that these members of parliament, more of them or the majority of them, were members of the party for democratic prosperity, PDP?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. In 1990 there was only one party. There weren't two political parties among the Albanians. That was in the first parliamentary election.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the party for democratic prosperity was the second registered political party in general after the introduction of the multi-party system in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the first Albanian political party. I don't know whether it was the second or the third in the Macedonian parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the president of this party at the time was Nevzat Halili. Secretary was Mithat Emini?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chairman was Nevzat Halili whereas the Secretary-General was Mithat Emini. Mithat Emini.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, the answer to my question is correct. Is this so?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the constitution of 1991 guarantees, guaranteed full quality and permanent co-habitation of the Macedonian people with the Albanians, the Turks, the Vlaks, the Roma, and other nationalities living in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. It wasn't guaranteed by that document. That's why the deputies for the party for democratic prosperity did not vote in support of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My question was whether this was guaranteed or not.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't guarantee.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P91, page ERN N001-8938-001; Macedonian version, ERN N001-8970-001. English version accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see before you, Witness, where it is stated: " Constitution, parliament of the Republic of Macedonia"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters didn't hear the comment.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you see that this is the preamble of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. In the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it, but I can't read clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the first paragraph be enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Sir, it is said: "Macedonia is constituted as a national state of the Macedonian people full equality and permanent co-habitation is secured of the Macedonian people with the Albanians, the Turks, the Vlaks, the Roma, and other nationalities living in the Republic of Macedonia." Do you see this before you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this preamble of the Republic of Macedonia guarantees full equality, civil equality, of all enumerated and non-enumerated nationalities living in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on how you interpret this preamble. I said it --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the same constitution which was also in power in 2001 in the units of local self-government where the majority or a substantial number was inhabited by members of the nationalities, in addition to the Macedonian language and the Cyrillic alphabet, the language and the alphabet of the nationalities were also in official use in a manner and under conditions determined by law?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. The Albanian language was not an official language.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P91, page 2, ERN number N001-8938-002; Macedonian version and ERN N001-8970-002 received as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I bring your attention to the paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Article 7, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Article 7 reads: "In the Republic of Macedonia, the official language is the Macedonian and Cyrillic alphabet." And it further states: "In the unit of local self-government where the -- where members of the local communities are a -- members of ethnic minorities are a majority apart from the Macedonian alphabet and the Cyrillic alphabet, the language and the alphabet of the ethnic minorities will be used in a manner established by law." And it further states that: "In the local self-government units where there is a significant number of residents belonging to the ethnic minorities, apart from the Macedonian language and Cyrillic alphabet, also the language and the alphabet of the minorities will be in official use under the circumstances and in a manner established by law." Is it correct that pursuant to Article 7 of the constitution, it is guaranteed, it is allowed the right to official use of other languages of the ethnic minorities, apart from the Macedonian language, where they are prevalent or where they are in a significant number, so even where there is a significant number?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still didn't give you my answer. Your Honours, please, let me answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what you're invited to do, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he just interrupted me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you're saying is not true. This preamble and it was precisely this Article that was changed, that was subject to change during the Ohrid Agreement. As I said earlier, it depends on how you interpret the constitution. The fact is that this, in reality, did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001 there was education in the Albanian language in all grades of the elementary, secondary and higher education?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one secondary school in Skopje in the Albanian language. It was Gymnasium Zef Lushmarku.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there a secondary school in Tetovo in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there a secondary school in the Albanian language in Gostivar?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there was. There should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there a secondary school, for instance, in Albanian language in Strumice?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Strumice?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, in Albanian, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you confirm through your evidence that in every city where there is Albanian population there was secondary education provided in Albanian language and in the city of Strumice where no Albanians live, of course, there is no Albanian language education?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But why, then, there is no secondary school in the Albanian in Manastir or Bitola where there are Albanians living? You cannot make such comparisons as far as education is concerned. When you only have one secondary school in the Albanian language, Zef Lushmarku in Skopje, when you have such a large figure of Albanian population in Skopje and there are only seven or eight classes teaching in Albanian in this secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001, the Macedonian Albanians had a pedagogical academy and dramatic arts academy in the Albanian language, as well as the theological Islamic faculty and the secondary Islam school?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secondary theological school, the Medresa and the theological faculty did exist. This pertains to the pedagogical academy as well, but at a university level there were only two universities in Macedonia: the University of Skopje and the University of Bitola and they were both Macedonian universities. We didn't have any Albanian university. You know very well that when the Tetovo university was established and which was self-financed by the Albanians just for them to be able to be educated in their native language, the Macedonian police took an action and went to Tetovo and killed the student with the last name Selimi. This is what happened. The Tetovo University became legal only after the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed, during the time of the coalition BDI, LSDM.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the beginning of 2001, also the South-eastern University --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: South-eastern Europe University, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: -- was opened in Tetovo and the teaching there was in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true not only in Albanian but in all languages. And it was not a university only in the Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You told my colleague Mettraux when he indicated that in 2001, in the Macedonian Assembly there were members of parliament who were Albanians. Is it true that they were elected in the free democratic elections in 1998?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ilijaz Sabriu was elected the vice-president of the assembly, a person of Macedonian nationality who was ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I don't remember who held this position, but from the beginnings of the Macedonian parliament and up until today, you always have this function. But you know that there are not only one vice-president or Speaker of the parliament, there are usually two or three and not only Albanians but also members of other communities. And this is subject to the political negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So for -- throughout the time since the independence of Macedonia there has been an ethnic Albanian as a vice-president of the Assembly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also, in the government of the Republic of Macedonia, in 2001, there were ministers of Albanian ethnicity. You also confirmed this with my colleague Mr. Mettraux. Is it correct that the deputy prime minister at the time was Bedredin Ibrahimi, Macedonian national of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is what I stated earlier that these posts of deputy Speaker and deputy prime minister existed but there are two or three deputies, not only one. And there is subject to negotiations between the ruling coalition parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that 20 per cent of the judges in the Supreme Court of the Republic of Macedonia, in 2001, were Albanians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I don't think that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001 there was also a large number of ambassadors of the Republic of Macedonia from the ethnic Albanian community, for instance I would enumerate here Alajdin Demiri, ambassador to Switzerland; Sami Ibraimi, ambassador to Denmark; Servet Ardiu, Croatia; and others?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a small number, but this is not important. What was important for us was the number of employees in the state administration and in the institutions. Let -- let's not deal with numbers of ministers and ambassadors which you can count on one hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the legally elected representatives of the Albanians in 2001 were against the terrorist group NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only Menduh Thaci and part of his party members.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Menduh Thaci and his party were elected in the elections 1998 to represent the interests of the Albanians in the parliament and they were in the parliament in 2001.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the Albanians are legitimately represented in the parliament by those who win the election. This is the only democratic way. The party that wins the election takes a seat in the parliament and legitimately represents the Albanian people. These people did not win the election at the time but it was the wish of the prime minister then Ljupco Georgievski, to take for his part Menduh Thaci. As I mentioned earlier, this government was not interested in politics but in business but this brought to the war in 2001. The party that loses the election cannot become a legitimate representative of the people because, in this case, the will of the people has been violated.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the DPA was actually the will of the Albanian people in 1998, because they won the majority of Albanian seats in the parliament in the elections of 1998?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you're not very familiar with this field. What you're saying is not true. The elections in 1998 were won by PPD [as interpreted] and not by PDSH.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: With regards to PDP or DPA, or Albanian abbreviation PDSH, will be dealt with later when we discuss the Framework Agreement. Is it correct that there were signatories to the Ohrid Framework Agreement, PDP and DPA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which agreement -- yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Menduh Thaci, vice-president of the DPA, stated publicly that NLA is just a gang of criminals?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that in 2001, and he says it today in 2007. But a true Albanian would never say that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Does it also correspond to the statements of renowned politicians such as George Robertson and Javier Solana?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it corresponds with the statement, but I will tell you again that we were a regular army and not criminals as Menduh Thaci used to call us then and now. We were a regular army with our uniform, with our emblem and with our rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My colleague Mettraux read to you that the terrorist organisation NLA had no support, neither by NATO nor the European Union. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall him asking me these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you aware that all NATO member states, as well as the 15 member states of the European Union, all of them have named or called your organisation NLA terrorists or group of thugs and murderers and they supported the Macedonian security forces to deal with your terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of these statements could be so, but not all what you're saying, sir. I have mentioned earlier that this was in the beginning of the war, and you probably know that the US, NATO, and the European Union were the guarantors of the Ohrid Agreement. How can they support terrorists? This really doesn't make sense to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You are saying that that was at the beginning of the war. In your opinion, what is that time, the beginning of the war, and until how long did this beginning last?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war began on 14th of February and ended with the demobilisation on the 26th of September. You know very well that there word "terrorist" did not appear on the Ohrid Framework Agreement why nobody from the Macedonian representatives wrote down on that document, on that agreement that we were terrorists. If we were such and if that word appeared on the Ohrid Framework Agreement, that agreement would never have been made. You must be aware of that, sir. And the Ohrid Agreement foresaw, envisaged an amnesty for the NLA members and the NLA leadership. In which country have you seen an example of terrorists being amnestied?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. We will discuss the Ohrid Framework Agreement later.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me the question now and I cannot answer to this question by saying yes or no only.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I asked you -- I'm asking you and you confirm that the war started on the 26th of February?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 14th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So which time-period do you consider to be this beginning of the war, the time that you were considered terrorists? Would this be until the 14th of March, for instance, that you considered the beginning? Could you please note which is the period that you yourself considered to be the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We consider the entire period war because we started the war, but we did not know at the time when the war would end, whether in 2001 or 2 or 3 or 4 or 5. We knew when the war began, but we didn't know then when it would end.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to show you now the video recording from a press conference of George Robertson, NATO Secretary-General and Javier Solana, High Representative for Foreign Security Policy of the European Union, dated 7th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. Could my learned colleague state the ERN or the 65 ter of this video for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video-clip does not have an ERN number but the Prosecution was informed in writing that we would use this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have any concern, Ms. Regue?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I would like to know the source because we were informed, in fact, about the title but to be honest we thought that there was a ERN on the video. We would like to know actually the source, the date of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you indicate the source and the date, please, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. 7th of May, 2001. And the source is the Macedonian Television as well as for the other evidence that the Prosecution has secured from the Macedonian Television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue with your playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] Ladies and gentlemen, there were quite extensive discussions with the President Solana and with ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I have two interpretations here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you wait until [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Apostolski, that has presented a significant problem because the witness has not been able to hear what was being said. He has had no translation because it's come from a video soundtrack, and therefore those two speeches have not reached him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now do we correctly understand that you were not able to follow this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, sir. But I was able to follow bits.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the video-clip was in English and with interpretation in Macedonian so we considered, considering that the witness speaks the Macedonian language that he would be able to understand the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can see the problem of introducing a video which is not in the system and for which there is no written transcript. Now what you're going to have to do if you want to cross-examine on any part of that is to give to the witness, at least orally, a translation of what is said at any particular point. Do you want to be asking in detail about aspects about what was said there?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I only wanted to show to the witness that Sir George Robertson and Sir Javier Solana did not support the NLA organisation and that the organisation NLA was called a group of thugs, murderers and terrorists. That was the point of this video-clip for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may be able to ask the witness whether he understood from what you heard of that and saw of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- if that was their message. If he didn't, it is going to be hard going from then on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, from what you understood from the video-clip, have you heard that Lord Robertson and Javier Solana did not support your organisation and that they called you a group of thugs, murderers and terrorists?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard some bits. I didn't hear them saying all these words. And secondly, I'm not saying that in the beginning of the 2001 war we had a full support, but I can tell you one thing, that the withdrawal of the NLA soldiers from Haracin village was carried out by the United States of America. This is a fact. I'm not saying that they supported us in combat with the Macedonian security forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I was wrong because I was taking notes when the video was playing, but I didn't any hear calling the NLA, well, this organisation a terrorist group either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I noted the words in one passage, "murderous thugs in hills to the north." I think at some other point the word "terrorist" was used, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe it was acts of terrorism but not terrorist organisation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Acts of terrorism may have been the case. But I think Mr. Apostolski has got the answer he was hoping for or looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that on the 13th of August, the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed. You had already stated this. Is it correct that the signatories to the Framework Agreement were Imer Imeri and Arben Xhaferi as legitimate representatives of the Albanians in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were representatives of the Albanian people, but not -- correction, of the Albanian political parties but not of the Albanian people in general. And it is true that they did sign this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that no NLA representative had signed the Framework Agreement in Ohrid?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that they did not sign it, but it was drafted by -- prepared by members of the NLA. So both Imeri and Xhaferi, they were just -- they were just there, present.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that no NLA representatives signed the Ohrid Framework Agreement, since NLA did not represent the interests of the Albanians and it was not supported by the international community? You yourself stated that the international community did not negotiate with terrorists.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the international community never negotiates with terrorists. I told you that they negotiated with us in a capacity of a regular army, and they negotiated with our political representative Mr. Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, do you think, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now, and we expect to be resuming at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in regards to the previous video-clip, we spoke with my colleagues of the Prosecution, so for the same video-clip, there will be a transcript made on our part and it will be uploaded in an electronic version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you understand the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you be shown a video-clip with titles in the Macedonian language? Would you be able to follow it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If that's going to happen, we need to turn off the microphones on the witness's desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness may be shown a video-clip with the statement of the Ambassador of Great Britain, Mark Dickenson, of April 2001. The source is Macedonian Television.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, could you agree with me that in his statement Mr. Mark Dickenson, Ambassador of Great Britain in Macedonia, called your organisations as extremists and terrorists, which want to introduce anarchy in the country by their terrorist acts?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from the former Ambassador Dickenson, but I'm convinced that the gentleman does not know the meaning of terrorism. And I said earlier these statements of the European and international representatives were at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ambassador Dickenson stated that your organisation does not have the support of 99 per cent of the population of the Albanians in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's different from what he states, and the reality is quite different. He couldn't have spoken on behalf of the Albanian people. He could speak as a representative of Britain and as an ambassador. But not as a representative of the Albanian people in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Mark Dickenson in his statement also mentions that the goals of your organisations are unclear because at one point federalisation of the state is requested, further on a constituent nation status is requested which is contrary to your statement for the goals of your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. What he says is not true. Our aims were quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your goals were?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main aim was a change in the constitution so that we could be a constituent nation and enjoy equal rights with other peoples.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me how many numbers -- how many people numbered the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but roughly I could say 5 to 6.000 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were members of the NLA from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the NLA there were members from everywhere. There were a small number of Kosovo, some from Albania, but there were also Roma who were members of the NLA, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is that small number from Kosovo? Do you know this figure, do you know this number?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say the exact number. In my brigade, I could say there was a small number, but I couldn't give any figures about other brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And they fought, as you yourself said, for changing the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They helped the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you please answer my question whether they fought for changing the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia because you said that the goals of your organisation was to change the Constitution of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that the number of NLA was 5.000 to 6.000 members. Is it correct that each one of them was equipped with infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that most frequently members of the NLA used Kalashnikovs of Chinese origin?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chinese and Russian.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that your brigade numbered a thousand people. Is it correct that each of one of them was disarmed with demoblisation, with the Harvest action?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that each member of the NLA was disarmed with the Operation Essential Harvest?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it possible that some of the soldiers did not hand over their weapons, members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that would have been possible because in order to take a certificate that the NLA was demobilised, one of the first items was to hand over the weapons. And that any member could not have handed over his weapon, I don't believe this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 2D00-367. This is a statement by Gezim Ostreni, page 10, paragraph 46 of the English version and page 9 of the Macedonian version. Paragraph 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see paragraph -- this paragraph 46 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 46? Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you read in it that it says: "Eventually every NLA member had a weapon. The number of weapons matched the number of soldiers. In Operation Harvest, 3.875 pieces of weapons were handed over by the NLA to NATO. It is possible that some soldiers did not hand over their weapons."

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your so-called chief of General Staff said that maybe all of them were not disarmed and that, as you said, if the NLA had 5 to 6.000 members and all of them had at least one piece of weapon, then the numbers which you state and the numbers which are mentioned by your head of General Staff do not match?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Didn't give an accurate number, I said it may be 5 to 6.000; it could be 4.000. And I also said that someone may not have handed over the weapon. And he is not the so-called Chief of Staff of the NLA but he's the Chief of Staff of -- of General Staff of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said -- Witness, earlier you said that every member of the NLA handed over the weapon. This was two minutes ago. And that this was obligatory in order for you to receive a certificate that you were an army. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's accurate, but I said that may be someone who had not handed over, but I don't believe it. That's what I said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Gezim Ostreni has said this in his statement while you here today testified that everybody handed over their weapon, but let us proceed. Is it correct that the NLA comprised of a number of brigades, you confirmed this, the 112, 113, 114, 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you implemented a coordinated operation that would include two or more brigades?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a genuine coordination with the 113rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So together with the 113 Brigade, you carried out joint operations. Is this what you testify before this Court?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not joint operations, but coordination as far as the front line was concerned. Joint front line we had -- we shared.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know in the period of 2001 whether any one of these brigades, which you so call, carried out a joint operation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There hasn't been in our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, each brigade acted independently -- independently of your General Chiefs of Staff?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct. We operated on the basis of the military hierarchy. We got our orders from the General Staff and from the chief of General Staff, Gezim Ostreni, General Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that each brigade fought in accordance with its own plan and assessment? Can you tell this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had our own plans, and on the basis of the circumstances. But on -- on many things, on certain things we had to coordinate our activities with General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you here testify that every brigade, each brigade worked in coordination, or with coordination of the chief of General Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown point 53, item 53, of Gezim Ostreni's statement which is already on the screen. Item 53. This is on page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see before you item 53? This is the statement of your chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At the end of item 53 it is said that: "Every brigade had an area (zone) of responsibility and each was fighting according to its own plan and judgement. We actually did not have a possibility to conduct any coordinated operations involving several brigades." Did your chief of General Staff in his statement say something contrary to which you have now testified?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying, but the General and myself are saying one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but I think Mr. Apostolski and the statement of Mr. Ostreni are dealing with different issues. I think that one issue is the coordination that each brigade would have with the General Staff; that's what the witness answered. And what Mr. Ostreni here says is joint coordination actions among the brigade, which is a second issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I leave it to you, Mr. Apostolski, whether you want to explore further on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that each member of the brigade had a uniform with the insignia of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the uniform -- they received the uniform when they joined your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. When they joined the brigade, when they took an oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, once they were in the brigade, they took a uniform and then they had an oath, they took an oath. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they took the uniform, they took an oath, and they underwent military training as laid out in the NLA rule book.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your commander Gezim Ostreni told you that a person without a uniform would be considered as a criminal, not as a fighter?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had it in our rule book that a member of the NLA would not go out and about without a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you adopted all military standards and procedures in establishing the brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You had rules for establishing a brigade, rules for mobilisation of a battalion, rules for commanding a brigade. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that these rules were received by you from the Chiefs of Staff -- from the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you adopted all the planned military standards and procedures during the establishment of your brigade.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And all the other brigades had adopted the planned military standards and procedures. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 2D00-367, page 6, paragraph 28, Macedonian and the English version. That is the statement of Gezim Ostreni given to the ICTY investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 28 -- can you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: He says that: "Because of the short period between March 2001 when I joined the NLA, and the beginning of August when Ohrid Agreement was signed, it was impossible to adopt all planned military standards and procedures." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that your head of -- chief of General Staff says something that is in contradiction with your evidence here, that you had adopted all planned standards and procedures?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With full responsibility, I am stating here that my brigade followed all the procedures and standards in the establishment of 114th Brigade. You asked me about my brigade. This could refer to the beginning of the war in Tanushevc when you're saying that someone did not follow these procedures. I'm here giving evidence about my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But I asked you about the other brigades and you stated that the other brigades had it done. Is that correct, do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But after I read to you the statement of your Chief of Staff, could you agree with me that it was not so?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So what your Chief of Staff has stated would be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see what he stated in his statement, the chief of General Staff, but I don't know which period of time he is referring to in this statement. The 114th Brigade was established on the 1st of July and you know this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will read once again that your chief of General Staff speaks about the time-period between 2001, when he joined the NLA and the beginning of August, when the Ohrid Agreement was signed. And further on, he states that during that period, it was impossible to adopt all planned military standards and procedures. Does that comprise the entire period of war that you are also speaking about?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the entire period, but it does not speak about 114th Brigade. You asked me about my brigade, and I can tell you with full responsibility that my brigade followed all the standards and procedures when it was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you managed to introduce those standards and procedures within four days, as you stated to my colleague Guenael that it took you four days to establish your brigade. Would that be your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My evidence is the following. The creation, the establishment of the staff of the brigade took three days, while the establishment of the brigade took the entire period up until the demobilisation. So throughout this period, we mobilised new soldiers, and this happened until the Ohrid Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated to my colleague when he cross-examined you yesterday that everyone in your brigade had ranks. Your deputy was Halil Paloshi. What was his rank? Are you able to say that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halil Paloshi?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer because of overlapping in the booth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the military formation of a brigade, he had the rank of a colonel, lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me about your head of logistics, Selam Hasani. What was his rank?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the formation, I think he was a captain or first class captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Commander of the military police was Jahi Nuhilu [as interpreted]. Can you tell me what was his rank?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nuhiju. I don't remember his rank exactly. I think he was a captain. But, as I said, I don't remember exactly. And this was in line with the formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the military police in your brigade had ever detained someone, a member of your brigade, for not observing the discipline?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me in relation to which event.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For failing to comply with the internal rules of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you run a disciplinary procedure against that person later, within your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't follow a disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You stated that Xhavit Hasani with nickname Marshall had the rank of a captain. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain or captain first class, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember at the beginning of your evidence you stated to my learned colleague from the Prosecution that you confirmed actually the ranks that your officers had in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P445. Exhibit P455.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see them in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. So do you remember now that you confirmed to my colleague that these were the ranks or the patches worn, depending on the rank, by your officers?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are not the emblems, but the ranks, the NLA ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It must have been a mistake in the interpretation. I asked you about the ranks.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. These are the ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the discipline and the management of operation of the NLA was decided based on the ranks?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officers were assigned ranks based on the military formation they led, and with time, through merit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it is correct that in the NLA from the very beginning that discipline and the management of operations were determined based on the ranks, or were the ranks respected at all in the operation of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't understand this question. I don't know if you formulated it correctly. What you're saying here is ranks and operations. What I told you is that the ranks were assigned based on the military formation, and later on, based on merit of soldiers or officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will reframe the question then. Was the hierarchy strictly observed, based on the ranks? Could a captain order a colonel?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That means that the hierarchy was strictly respected, the hierarchy in ranks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now it's okay. I agree, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you agree with me, then, that in the NLA the discipline and the management in its operation and its functioning were determined based on the ranks?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 2D00-3667, page 6, paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It is again a statement by your chief of General Staff Gezim Ostreni, who in paragraph 28, towards the middle. Can you see it? There's -- there it is at the beginning where it is written. That he says: "From the very beginning, the management and discipline in the NLA were not determined based on the ranks but according to the hierarchy of the position." Do you see this in front of you? Do you see this in front of you, what I have just read?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that your so-called commander, the chief of General Staff, speaks something that is in complete contradiction with you, that the hierarchy was not exactly observed based on the ranks, as you assert it were?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm stating here things about 114th Brigade. As I said earlier, the 114th Brigade was established on the 1st of July and there was time for all these things to be followed. And as far as I can see, the General Gezim Ostreni not speaking about the 114th Brigade. It is true that in the beginning we didn't have barracks, but as time went by we had everything. His statement speaks of the beginning. It says from the beginning. When you're asking me about 114th Brigade, I will reply accordingly because I have facts as far as my brigade is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me to interrupt, but I -- but maybe it will assist if the Defence counsel can read the following three lines that may assist also the witness to understand what Gezim Ostreni was meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the other lines I could read them, but I don't think they are related to my question, because I asked the witness previously whether the hierarchy was strictly observed as determined by the rank system. So it states further: "Therefore in the NLA it was common when addressing a senior member to address him with the functional position, like, for instance, brigade commander rather than with the rank corresponding to this position." So what follows is only an explanation of the way of addressing and not the way of functioning. So I think that it is unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not like you're reading it, sir. It says from the very beginning the functional and disciplinary authority in the NLA. As I said earlier, the 114th Brigade was established on 1st of July and by that time, all the preparations were already made.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that actually the ranks in the NLA did not really depict the actual position in the brigades, in terms of who has seniority in them?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. The ranks were assigned based on the military formation and based on the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that although you were the so-called commander of the 114th Brigade, it was actually Xhavit Hasani the one who said what is to be done and he was the highest authority in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I was not a so-called commander. I was a commander while Xhavit Hasani was the officer responsible for morale and information. I was the person in charge of my brigade. If we're talking about respect here, I was a well-respected person, while personally I also had respect for Mr. Xhavit Hasani due to his age and due to his experience in previous wars in Kosova and Presevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But is it correct that the highest authority for the 114th Brigade was precisely Xhavit Hasani?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you're saying is not true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Is it correct that you issued orders for terrorist actions to be performed in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. And which terrorist action are you referring to in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that within your so-called brigade there was also the sabotage unit of Lefta Goxhaj, aka Teli?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a unit, a reconnaissance sabotage unit, called Teli within the framework of 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it then your evidence that this is a sabotage unit?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reconnaissance sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Lefter Goxhaj, Teli, was an Albanian from Albania. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And he came to Macedonia to fight for the change of constitutional order in Macedonia, because that was the aim of your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To your information, Lefter Goxhaj, aka Teli, was a soldier who took part in three wars in Kosova, Presevo and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So he was a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a soldier with great experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But at any rate, he was a professional soldier, and he did not come to Macedonia in order to overthrow the constitution.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to assist the war, and you have to be clear on one thing. No one came and joined the NLA for money or for daily allowances, which was the case with the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Teli was getting ready to carry out sabotage actions in Skopje in order to kill civilian population and cause panic, because he was an experienced soldier?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. Our reconnaissance sabotage unit was not there to fight civilians but to fight directly the armed Macedonian forces, police and army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And he did this by entering the centre of Skopje together with his group on the 6th of August armed with weapons, bombs, explosives. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, he entered Skopje, he did not kill civilians on the 6th of August when he entered Skopje. It was a reconnaissance sabotage unit and we were ready for every option available to us in case the Ohrid Agreement was not signed. To take up to plan B and that was to proclaim free territories which were in the area of responsibility of the 114th Brigade. Unfortunately, they were not caught in action. Teli and his groups were sleeping in a house in Gazi Baba and the police, with a special unit, went and killed them all. You should know one thing: The house where these NLA soldiers were killed, a civilian, a member of a certain family was taken from that house and his whereabouts remain unknown. The police is the one who took this civilian. And, sir, you have to be held responsible for the very fact that he has disappeared and cannot be found for six years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your plan B, as you call it, was to plant mines and explosives around the territory of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true. Plan B was to expand the territories in the area of responsibility of 114th Brigade. As I mentioned in the beginning, the operational area differed from the area of responsibility. Skopje was part of the area of responsibility of the 114th Brigade, but the plan was not to plant mines and to do whatever you're saying here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the group of Teli was also wearing uniforms, as you gave evidence that all members of your brigade were wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that in the operational area each and every member of the NLA wore a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And according to your evidence of yesterday, they were not wearing uniforms in the urban areas or in the settlements, because you testified yesterday that Teli went to Skopje without wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not wear uniforms on them but they had the uniforms. They were carrying them with them. You know very well that they had the uniforms, they had the weapons. They were not ordinary civilians walking around Skopje. They were part of a reconnaissance sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So your present evidence is that they were armed in Skopje but without wearing uniforms. They had the uniforms with them but not wearing them. They were -- the uniforms were hidden somewhere.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not armed in Skopje proper. They had the uniforms when they set out from Nakustak. They had the uniforms with them as well. However, the media -- when I saw them killed, I saw that they were not wearing the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday to my colleague Guenael that it would be illogical to wear uniform when entering the city of Skopje or any other settlement, that it would be illogical to enter there wearing uniforms. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this and it is quite illogical, I abide by my previous statement. I'm not saying that they changed their clothes on the street, that they put on civilian uniforms -- dress, sorry, or uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also, you gave evidence just now that the group from Nikustak, Teli's group came armed with weapons? Do you recall this? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They set out armed and in uniforms. It is possible that they changed their clothes on the way. I don't know whether they left the weapons or they took them with them in Skopje. We were organised in a totally different way from what you think, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript of 5682 [as interpreted] you stated that they set out with arms. I say this for the purpose of the record. Could the witness please be shown video-clip 5364, received in evidence. The number has been noted wrongly. The transcript page is 5862, not as stated 5682. This 5364, this is the video-clip 5364 received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please stop the video here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise these persons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the person lying on his stomach with a beard. It should be Arben. I can't see the other two very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see that they're clothed in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the group of Commander Teli?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I see here, Arben, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that from Nikustak they did not set out dressed in civilian clothing as you see them here when you saw them. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know if you refuse to understand or it is really not clear to you. I already told you that they set out with uniforms. It is possible that in Skopje they changed their clothes and put on civilian clothes. This is what I already told you. I told you, as well, that they had weapons with them. They had sniper, they had a Kalashnikov, they had a hand-held mortar. You should tell me one thing here. Where is the member of that family in that house, that civilian who was not even a member of the NLA who disappeared? He was just a civilian member of the family where these persons were staying that night. You should give me an answer to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, they came to a civilian house. They were staying in a civilian house. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did they go to Skopje on your order?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Why is it that you cannot say?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a personal thing. Still there are certain things unclear surrounding Commander Teli's death. I think that his death was a result of a betrayal and there is an investigation still ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
