utterances.text: Therefore, you do not want to tell me whether they started out towards Skopje on your order. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the video -- can we please go on with the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You say that the village of Ljuboten was not of interest to you. Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You explain this with the fact that the logistics of your so-called brigade came from Aracinovo. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that your brigade was established at the beginning of July. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As a continuation of 113rd brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Aracinovo was under the control of the Macedonian security forces from 26th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't entirely under the control of the Macedonian forces. It was a multi-ethnic police force at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the case of the Defence is that Ljuboten was the most important thing was where their logistics came from, from ONA over the village [as interpreted]. There were members of the NLA in the village, in uniform, black and camouflage uniforms but also in civilian clothes as you saw them previously shown to you so that they may not be noticed by the security forces by which they would support the most -- they would lose the most important point of logistics. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. I told you a day earlier, show me one soldier who killed -- show me one single NLA soldier dressed in uniform who was killed in Ljuboten. You know what you did. Two years ago you took an amount of weapons to a house in Ljuboten and then you told the world that this is what we found here. Whilst you conducted the search you didn't find anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I just want you to -- to put it to you that even on the video-clip you just saw previously that the people which I showed to you, although members of your brigade, they were in civilian clothes not in uniforms. But my question is: Was your brigade at the location of Matejce and Lipkovo. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, before I answer this question, I'll go back to the previous one. You should play on that video-clip because they had weapons with them, where as Erxhan Aliu in Ljuboten did not have any weapons. All of those people who were killed there, they didn't have any weapons; they had something with them. But in the case of Gazi Baba, they had weapons and if you play that video on, you will see the weapons. As far as the 114th Brigade, we didn't have representatives in Likov; in Matejce, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall we see the rest of the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For your brigade, was in the area of Matejce --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we please see the rest of the video so that the Honoured Judges can see what I'm saying? Can -- can we see that, so that this Chamber can see that they had weapons with them, whereas in Ljuboten, those who were killed, they did not have any weapons with them. This is the comparison I'm trying to make. You are only showing those bits which are favourable to what you want to say. Like you said, you brought here to court just the statements from Solana and Dickenson.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can we continue, witness?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you do what I'm asking so that I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reply. Are you going to play the rest of the video involving Teli? You are not giving an answer to what I'm saying. Will you continue to play the rest of the video regarding Teli in Gazi Baba so that we can see for ourselves that they had weapons. Otherwise, I won't reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This video-clip has been received in evidence by this Court.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, will you please understand that your role here is to assist the Chamber to try and find out what went on. The process involves your being questioned by the Prosecution, cross-examined by Defence counsel, and then you will be re-examined by the Prosecution. Now, if there are matters which are considered to be important to the full understanding of what you're saying which do not emerge during your cross-examination by Defence counsel, then Prosecution counsel can go to those matters again and bring them out. So you have made the point to Mr. Apostolski that a part of the video which he has shown does not disclose that there were weapons. We have in fact seen that full video earlier, before you came to give evidence. We're seeing it again at the moment. So I would suggest you listen to the questions an answer them, and if it's thought to be important to the Prosecution, Ms. Regue will go over that matter again in re-examination. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much, Your Honour. I'm ready to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your brigade was in the area of Matejce. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Matejce and Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me in Lipkovo. Who was in Lipkovo?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Lipkovo, it was the 113rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that one of the cultural monuments of -- one of the cultural values of the Albanians is honesty and loyalty?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that an Albanian would never break an oath given to another?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be, but to this day things have changed. It should be that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the woman is the pillar of the Albanian family and is characterized by honesty?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it characteristic of the Albanian woman to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it -- if an Albanian woman were to say that the village of Ljuboten is the logistics centre of the NLA, would you believe this woman?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may or may not believe her. As I said earlier, it should be that way, but today things have changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the statement of Ismaili Tenzile, 65 ter 2D00-374, page 4, paragraph 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see this -- can you see the Macedonian version in front of you, paragraph 15. In her statement given to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal on 3rd of October 2004, it is said: "I do not know whether somebody from the village was a member of the NLA but as far as I know, the road Kumanovo-Lipkovo was blocked and journalists that wanted to reach Lipkovo walked through the mountains from Ljuboten. I have not seen anyone from the NLA in the village."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the English page be switched.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "As villagers we prepared the food for the NLA, but I personally never saw any of them in the village. The volunteers from the village were collecting logistics from the Ljuboten villagers and they transported it to the mountains. For example, my brother-in-law, Xhemal Ismaili and others took care of this, but I do not know their names. I was not very much familiar with. This they transported food and other necessary things to Lipkovo and Matejce." Can you agree with me that Ms. Tenzile Ismaili from Ljuboten speaks the truth?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tenzile Ismaili is saying the truth when she says that there was no NLA in Ljuboten. As far as the food for our soldiers, we had our own kitchens.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So, in the first two sentences she is lying, or rather, is telling the truth and is lying -- and is not telling the truth in the other sentences. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She is telling the truth about what she saw with her own eyes. She said that she didn't see any NLA soldiers and the rest she said that she'd heard about things.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In concrete terms, she says that her brother-in-law Ismaili took care of this and that they transported the food and other necessary things on horses to Lipkovo. She confirms the arguments of the Defence that Ljuboten was a logistics centre for your brigade and also for the 113 Brigade which was in Lipkovo as you just said. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I will say a few more things. This is not correct. If that was correct, if there were such things true, you would have had information from the secret services from the Ministry of Interior. And I'm sure that you'd have captured those people in Ljuboten. But there was no hostages in Ljuboten, no NLA soldiers there. You only quote statements. You do not deal with facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Remember when you say that you were never in Ljuboten. You were never in Ljuboten in that period of time, or at least this was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true I wasn't there. In 2001, I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you cannot testify about what happened in Ljuboten in 2001.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that if there was such a thing in Ljuboten, you would have acted. Why didn't you capture an NLA soldier in uniform there? Or weapons? You have not done this. You -- you had information but you [Indiscernible] to do their own thing. This is illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the army stopped your logistic channels from Ljuboten, you decided, you reached a decision to threaten them by planting mines and carrying out a terrorist act so that these roads may be cleared up?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purpose of the transcript I would point out the testimony of Jurisic and Despodov.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to answer this question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not correct, what Mr. Apostolski is saying. As far as the planting of the mine -- [Microphone not activated] The planting of the mine was a lack of -- [Microphone not activated] That is between the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This last answer, I'm afraid was not fully recorded and it is not been fully interpreted. I wonder whether you would mind repeating your answer, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said what Mr. Apostolski is saying is not correct. The planting of the mine may have been the result of a lack of coordination between the Macedonian army and police when there was a conflict between the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Defence, and I have never issued any orders to plant any mines in Ljuboten or above Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry, Mr. Apostolski, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, might this be a good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume, then, at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall that I asked you whether you had issued an order to plant the mine at Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you had issued orders for any actions that your brigade carried out. That is 5057, page 5637 of the transcript. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You also stated that you received orders from the General Staff, from Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For things that were not clear to us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the action of Teli in Skopje, the reconnaissance action and information gathering action, was based on your order?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already stated, I will not answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you would not answer the question?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the reasons that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I put it to that you that you had issued an order for Teli to enter Skopje, since you had issued all orders at the level of your brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you please tell me whether your brigade had under its control any railway station?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did it have under its control any highway?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did it have any city under its control?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In your evidence, you mentioned several times that the Macedonian forces have carried out at least two massacres of Albanian civilians. In your opinion, that was an alleged massacre against a father and a son in Tetovo and the alleged massacre in the village of Ljuboten. Page 5793, 5796, 5849 of the transcript. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. But I said they killed them and that it was a massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You told us that the father and the son were killed although they were unarmed and were not wearing uniforms. In yesterday's transcript, page 5849, line 22. Do you stay with this statement?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. And this is the truth, this is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 2D379.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this one of those photographs?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the photograph of the event in Kosova --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- where the son and the father were killed just in front of the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I put it to that you willingly give false evidence before this Court in order to blacken the security forces and save the face of the NLA members to present them as civilians. You are saying -- doing this in both relation to the Tetovo case as well as the Ljuboten case. I will now show you other images from this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter photograph 2D376.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I answer this question before we go to the next picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's fair enough, Mr. Apostolski. You made a big assertion and then have not allowed the witness to comment on it. So, yes, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, if we can go back to the first picture, the one before this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the photograph 65 ter 2D379.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, with full responsibility, I'm stating this because not only myself but the entire world, the entire Albanian people, and whoever followed the media at that time were clear on one thing, that the father and the son had no weapons with them and no uniforms on them. Secondly, I'm here to tell the truth before this Tribunal, and to tell you that a crime was committed against the villagers of Ljuboten. What we see on this photograph is just one of examples of what happened there. On 9th of June in the house of Metush Ajeti, he was taken from his own house to the police station and his body was later on disposed. Where are the other persons who were stopped at check-points? Where were they taken to? This is not a false evidence that I'm giving. This is the truth and it is supported by facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will show you now other photographs from this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 65 ter photograph 2D376. These are photographs taken by BBC.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the same event?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then show the next photograph, 2D377.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the person on the left-hand side wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And do you see what that person does and what is the person holding in his hand?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that he is holding something in the hand, in his hand, but I don't know what it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on the person on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it clearly. I see that he is holding something, but I can't see what. Please help me if you can see it clearly. If you know clearly what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it maybe resemble a bomb?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that. Had it been a bomb it would have exploded. Because at the moment when it was supposed to be thrown, it should have been activated and it would have been -- it would exploded, but this is not happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom out on the photograph so that we see the entire photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask counsel and witness to avoid overlapping for the sake of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, can you see now that the uniformed persons are running away from that person?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this was not the first time for them to run away. They always ran away.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if it had been a bomb, would they be running away?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. If this is a bomb, it would have exploded while he is holding in it in the hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And if he throws the bomb it can explode.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both if he throws it or if he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask once again for the counsel and witness to wait for the interpretation to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we seek to tender this photograph in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you just wait a moment, please. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I will ask, actually, the relevance of this photo, this particular photo to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance goes towards discrediting this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, this is a Prosecution submission that is quite a broad statement that my learned colleague has made. Discrediting this witness in regards with which particular issue and based on one photo that we are speculating what he had in his hand or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D49, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to say something about what this person is holding in his hand and what the lawyer asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, if this was a bomb, it was activated and it would have exploded because it is only for four our five seconds between the moment of activation and explosion. So it would have exploded whether it was thrown or still in his hand. So that's why I don't think it is a bomb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown a video-clip of the event secured from the Prosecutor, VOOO-6742-1-A. It starts with 58:59 and it goes until 59:19. So could we please play the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Even after the ultimatum, the terrorists did not give up on their intentions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have lost the sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can stop here. Could we please rewind it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you see what this is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you confirm that this is a bomb, a hand-grenade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not look like a hand-grenade to me and does not necessarily mean that this object is the same with the object that the person was holding in his hand. You can rewind the clip once again. And my question is, if it was a hand-grenade, why didn't it explode?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 65 ter 2D382. That is a analysis of the event produced by the BBC and the title is "Dual Vision in Macedonia."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Double vision," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the subtitle is people have different views on the death of the two ethnic Albanians. Could we see the second page of it, please. At the bottom of that page it says: "For the Macedonians, the two Albanians were terrorists who tried to kill their soldiers and deserved to be shot. But the word in the Albanian cafes was that it was not a hand-grenade but a mobile phone." And further on page 3 it states --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to page 3. "In a man's hand that caused him to be killed. And it says further on: "The images were very poor." It is further down under the subtitle, "sensitive issue." "The pictures were poor and you couldn't make out the objects in the man's hands. A soldier looked as though he was executing the two men. It looked bad, very bad. Knowing the sensitivity of the issue, I went to a BBC office and looked at the television footage of the shooting on a BBC monitor in at an extremely slow motion. This time the picture was clear. The Albanians had hand-grenades. They did throw them at the Macedonians who shot them, not in cold blood but in a frenzy of fear because they were under attack. "The British army would have done the same in Northern Ireland."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that the civilians with hand-grenades attacked the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that they had no hand-grenades and they did not carry out an attack of that nature. Sir, if they had a hand-grenade that would have gone off and you would have seen it in the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And if it were some other object, would the security forces who were armed with automatic rifles would they be running away from them?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. You should know better.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be logical if they're attacked with a hand-grenade, they would be running away, the security forces?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't it be logical for this hand-grenade to go off, to explode?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And otherwise the Prosecution witness Franz Hutch spoke about this at the page 2150 on the transcript of July 2007 and it says in it: "You must be aware that in Tetovo in March 2001, there has been an incident when the two NLA members were crossing a police check-points when they were stopped and they starting throwing hand-grenades at the police." So do you still maintain after all this, before this Chamber that this is a massacre similar to the one in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please show the video-clip -- could we seek to tender the video-clip that we had seen in evidence, VOOO-6742-A, 58:59 to 59:19.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it was secured through the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to repeat the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number please, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, VOOO-6742-1-A, 58:59 to 59:19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D50, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we also tender the BBC article, analysis of the event 65 ter 2D382. Can we seek to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis do you see a BBC investigation going to be helpful to us, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was thinking whether to tender this into evidence, but I do believe that it is in accordance with the event and to the fact that the argument of the Defence was that members of the NLA were dressed in civilian clothes when they were entering towns, and also an argument of our Defence is that civilian members of the NLA were in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the relevant part of this article have already been read in the transcript. And what has been read actually it is not stated clearly whether these two people were actually NLA members dressed in civilian clothings, at least from the text of the article. As I mentioned, it has already been read in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D51, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that it was obligatory for members of the NLA to use uniforms and that this uniform was issued upon membership or joining the NLA. Do you recall saying this? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The case of the Defence is that the NLA used civilian clothes as a tactics in order to carry out successfully attacks and then to run away and mix among the civilian population. They were not an army at all, rather, terrorists which had several uniforms from UCK from Kosovo to which they adhered the emblems of the NLA in Macedonia. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you, sir. According to you, was there any NLA in Manastir? Why did you deport the civilians? Why did you burn down the mosque there?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The case of the Defence that members of the NLA were also children below the age of 14 and people above the age of 65. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, sir. You're trying to reason for the killing of the seven-year-old and nobody will believe you about that -- Aliu, the name of the child [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the UCK in Kosovo and Macedonia used similar emblems and abbreviations?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- in Macedonia we had the National Liberation Army, whereas in Kosova they had the KLA and the emblems were different. We had the red-and-black emblem here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown picture 65 ter number 2D00-204.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the emblem of the NLA in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown picture 65 ter number 2D00-217 without closing this picture, so that we can compare the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the emblem of the UCK of the KLA in Kosovo, the yellow and red in colour, and black.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it earlier, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree that the emblems are the same, the abbreviation is the same, the form is the same, the differences are in colour and the form of the letters, black in one, yellow in the other and one says Kosovo Liberation Army and the other says National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is in the colour and in ours it says the National Liberation Army and in the Kosovo case, it's the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you would agree with me on this, that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me why these two are so similar?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are similar because both of them were armies, and there is -- the red of the flag, and the eagle is part of the national flag. And I said earlier, it's the same flag in Albania, Macedonia and in eastern Kosovo, and Kosovo itself, and in Montenegro. The Albanians have one flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you believe that without logistics from Kosovo and from UCK from Kosovo and the Kosovo Protection Corps, that it would be possible to carry out successful terrorist attacks in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. We had logistical support from Kosova and we had moral support from people who fought in the KLA and they supported the NLA and the same happened in Kosova. There were Macedonians who helped out with the war in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means -- this means that the UCK from Kosovo gave you support to realise your goals by logistics for the constitutional -- for taking down the constitutional order of the Republic of Macedonia which you said were the goals of your organisations.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there was only the Kosovo Liberation Army and I did not say that they have given direct support. They have helped out, and they were members of the National Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these emblems were given to members of the UCK at the beginning of 2001 and that prior to this there were no members from the UCK from Kosovo with emblems such as these? This is the emblem on the left side, which is the emblem of the UCK in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct that it came from there. This is the insignia of the National Liberation Army in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you -- I assume you're wanting both, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Both photographs the one on the left and the one on the right, with the aim of identifying them both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we need to receive them separately Mr. Apostolski. They will each be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 2D204 will become Exhibit 2D52. 65 ter 2D217 will become Exhibit 2D53, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is it time, perhaps, for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is time for the day to end, Mr. Apostolski. We continue tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
